Spirit Commands

SP costs come from the game data (cost table at ROM 0x100AD0, ordered by Spirit Command ID), and each effect is verified in code: a command can be cast as long as SP is at least the cost; “until next turn” means it's cleared for everyone when the next turn begins, so an effect used in the player phase lasts through the whole enemy phase. Compared with Akurasu, the descriptions of Trust, Faith, Resupply, Accel, Valor/Soul, Cover and Taunt differ, and many conditions Akurasu doesn't list are added.

Spirit Command list

NameSP costTargetDurationEffect
Self-Destruct1SelfInstantDestroys yourself, dealing damage equal to your current HP to every unit adjacent up, down, left or right (including allies), ignoring armor, terrain and barriers; units in Stealth take no damage, Libra takes only 10; unusable with no adjacent unitsNot on Akurasu
Scan11 enemyInstantView the target's status; usable only on enemies you have not yet fought or used Scan on, and the status stays visible afterwardNot on Akurasu
Accel10SelfNext moveDiffers from AkurasuMove +3; kept as long as you don't move, not cleared at turn change
Mercy10SelfOne battleIf the target has 20 HP or more and your Skill is strictly higher than theirs, the attack won't destroy them, leaving 10 HP; also works on counterattacksNot on Akurasu
Focus15SelfUntil next turnHit and evasion rates +30%
Flash15SelfUntil one evadeNot on AkurasuCompletely evades one enemy attack; Flash takes priority when it meets Bullseye; stays until you're attacked, even across turns
Vigor20SelfInstantRestores 30% of own max HP (rounded down); can't be used at full HP
Gain20SelfOne battleExperience ×2 from the next battle
Bullseye25SelfUntil next turn100% hit rate, ignoring the target's Afterimage and Parry; if the target used Flash, Flash takes priority; Dummy can still block itNot on Akurasu
Trust301 ally (self allowed)Not on AkurasuInstantRestores 30% of the chosen unit's max HP (rounded down)Differs from Akurasu
Wall30SelfUntil next turnDoubles own armor (doubled armor goes into the damage formula)Not on Akurasu
Cover351 ally (not self)Until attacked onceDiffers from AkurasuThe next time the chosen ally is attacked, you fight in its place, at any range; does not cover an ally that used Flash; ends if you are shot down or either unit boards, combines or uses Separate; no turn limit
Taunt351 enemyUntil it wears offDiffers from AkurasuMakes the chosen enemy target only you, at any range; it lasts until you are shot down, or either side boards, combines or Separates, with no turn limit; some bosses and elites are immune to TauntNot on Akurasu
Valor40SelfOne battleDiffers from AkurasuDamage ×2 in the next battle (counterattacks included); can't be used while Valor or Soul is active
Spirit40SelfInstantAll pilots of the unit get Will +10 (max 150)
Guts40SelfInstantFully restores own HP; unusable at full HP
Fortune45SelfOne battleFunds ×2 from the next battle (multiplied with the kill bonus; at most 65,535 per unit destroyed)
Daunt501 enemyInstantTarget enemy unit's pilots all get Will −10, down to a minimum of 50; the target's main pilot must have Will 51 or higherNot on Akurasu
Soul60SelfOne battleDiffers from AkurasuDamage ×3 in the next battle (counterattacks included); doesn't stack with Valor — an active Valor is cancelled on use (the SP spent on Valor is wasted)Not on Akurasu
Stealth60SelfUntil next turnCan't be attacked by enemies, and targets can't counter its attacks; self-destructs can't hurt it eitherNot on Akurasu
Zeal60SelfInstant+1 action remaining this turn; used before acting, you can act twice this turn
Resupply651 ally (not self)InstantFully restores the target unit's EN and all ammo, at any range; Will is unchangedDiffers from Akurasu
Rouse701 ally (self allowed)Not on AkurasuInstantTarget unit's pilots all get Will +10 (max 150)
Disrupt70All enemiesUntil next turnHalves the hit rate of every enemy on the map (third parties included), on counterattacks too; Bullseye and Flash are unaffected
Faith70All alliesDiffers from AkurasuInstantAll ally units on the map with HP not full (including self) recover 50% of max HP
Love90All alliesInstantAll ally units on the map (including self) fully recover HP
Enable901 ally (not self)InstantLets 1 unit that has already acted this turn act again
Miracle100SelfInstantThe in-game description is “????”; it actually triggers Guts, Spirit ×3, Accel, Bullseye, Flash, Soul and Fortune in turn, skipping any already active; costs only 100 SP
Prayer1001 ally (not self)InstantEach pilot on the target unit recovers 50 SP (up to the maximum)
Revive1201 allyInstantChoose 1 destroyed ally unit to Revive beside you: HP, EN, ammo and SP fully restored, Will back to 100 (+5 per equipped Shuffle Crest), spirit effects cleared, and it can act this turnNot on Akurasu
  • “Duration” follows when the code clears the effect: Accel clears after the next move; Focus, Wall, Bullseye, Disrupt and Stealth clear for everyone when the turn count increases (the next turn); Valor, Soul, Fortune, Gain and Mercy clear after one battle ends, for both attacker and defender; Flash and Cover clear after triggering; Taunt lasts until a cancel condition occurs
  • Status-type Spirit Commands are recorded on the unit's main pilot, and ones used by sub-pilots also apply to the whole unit; the three pilots of a Getter-type unit share one set of statusesNot on Akurasu
  • When a Spirit Command changes Will, it is capped at 150 and floored at 50Not on Akurasu
  • Points where Akurasu disagrees with the code: Trust (Akurasu: restores 2000), Faith (Akurasu: restores half HP to one ally), Resupply (Akurasu: target's Will −10; the Will drop actually comes from the unit command “Resupply” — the Spirit Command Resupply doesn't lower it), Accel (Akurasu: lasts 1 turn), Valor/Soul (Akurasu: one attack), Cover and Taunt (Akurasu: one battle)Differs from Akurasu
  • The enemy AI never uses Spirit Commands on its own; any Spirit Command effects on enemies come from story commands and cost no SPNot on Akurasu
  • The game data also has an unnamed Spirit Command no. 31 that nobody can learn: cost 1, own Will +30; never used in normal playNot on Akurasu

Details verified in code

  • Flash takes priority over Bullseye: the hit check first looks at whether the defender has Flash — if so, it's 0% outright — and only then at the attacker's Bullseye
  • Bullseye sets hit rate straight to 100%, unaffected even by the halving when the defender picks the “Evasion” command; it also skips the Afterimage and Parry checks, but Dummy, barriers such as Aura Barrier and I-Field, and Shield still applyDiffers from AkurasuNot on Akurasu
  • Focus is symmetric: +30 hit when attacking, −30 to the attacker's hit when attacked
  • Disrupt marks every enemy; marked enemies have their hit rate halved when attacking and countering, stacking with the halving from the “Evasion” command (down to 1/4 at most)
  • Wall counts the defender's armor at 2× in the damage formula; it doesn't halve damage
  • Soul (×3) and Valor (×2) don't stack; with both active Soul applies; no criticals while either is active
  • Mercy compares both sides' Skill and requires yours to be strictly higher; it has no effect if the target has under 20 HP, so the target may be shot downNot on Akurasu
  • HP restored is max HP × the rate, fractions dropped
  • The hit roll is 1–99, so 99% and 100% hit rates have the same effect in practice

Pilot skills

All skill values come from ROM tables and battle code. In the original, several skills' code does not match their descriptions; this port's “Gameplay adjustments” turn these fixes on by default, and you can switch each one off on the “Rules” page of the settings to restore original behavior.

Skill effects: original and this port

SkillsEffectOriginal behaviorThis port's default
NT / EnhancedHit and evasion rise with level; can use NT-only weapons; Funnel-type range increasesHit and evasion at L1–L9: +10, 14, 18, 21, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30; Funnel, Fin Funnels, Mother Funnel and Reflector Bit need L1 to use, the MAP versions need L4; at L7 and L8 the 11 Funnel-type weapons get +1 max range, at L9 +2; Reflector Bit gets no range bonusNot on AkurasuSame as the original
Aura BattlerRaises evade and Aura Barrier; L1 enables Aura Slash, L3 enables Hyper Aura Slash and other weaponsRegardless of level, always −32 to the enemy's hit when attacked (even at skill level 0, before it shows on the status page); no modifier when attacking; Hyper Aura weapons get no power bonus; the Aura Barrier threshold rises with level (see “Unit Status”)Evasion by level: L1 +10 … L9 +30 (same curve as NT); the power of Hyper Aura Slash, Hyper Aura Cannon, Hyper Aura Shot Arm and Twin Aura Attack gets a level bonus: L3 +600, L4 +800, L5 +1000, L6 +1200, L7 +1300, L8 +1400, L9 +1500 (the normal Aura Slash doesn't)
ESPRaises hit and evade (the description also mentions attack power)Regardless of level: +64 hit when attacking, −64 to the enemy's hit when attacked; the attack power bonus doesn't exist at all in the original codeHit and evasion by level: L1 +10 … L9 +30; the attack power bonus is still not implemented
PotentialThe lower the HP, the higher the hit, evasion and critical ratesAll bands shift one step earlier: there is already a bonus at 90%+ HP (L9 +10), and the top band is reached below 20% HP; hit, evade and critical get the same value, up to +90 at L9No bonus at full HP (90%+); the top band only below 10% HP; hit and evade bonuses are halved (up to +45 at L9), critical unchanged (up to +90)
ParryWhen the unit carries a sword-type weapon, blocks an attack completely by chancePlayer side level÷16 (actually 57% at L9), enemy side level÷32 (actually 29% at L9); works only on weapons marked “parryable”: Missile, Torpedo, grenades and other solid-ammo weapons, plus about two thirds of Melee weapons; Beam weapons, vulcan-type shooting, and some Melee finishers such as Sekiha Tenkyoken and Burning Finger cannot be parried; does not trigger when the attacker uses BullseyeDiffers from AkurasuSame as the original
ShieldWhen the unit carries a shield, halves damage by chanceChance is the same as Parry (player ÷16, enemy ÷32, regardless of the incoming weapon); halved damage is rounded down to a multiple of 10, minimum 10; does not trigger on damage under 20; Bullseye cannot bypass it; not checked once Aura Barrier is broken throughDiffers from AkurasuSame as the original
Super Mode / Meikyo Shisui / BerserkAt Will 130 or higher, activates automatically when the specified pilot is in the specified GundamDomon, Argo, Sai Saici, George, Chibodee (only while on your side) and Master Asia, each in his own Gundam, switch to S/H mode at Will ≥130: max HP / EN +200/+50 (current values rise proportionally), mobility +10, limit +10, unit and weapon land, sea and space ratings become A (air unchanged), all pilot stats +10 and all pilot terrain ratings A, and their signature finishers gain attack power by pilot level (see the table below); the Burning Gundam H also gains God Shadow. An enemy Allenby in the Noble Gundam goes into Berserker mode, with only the unit bonuses. Once triggered it isn't cancelled by Will dropping — only when the unit is shot downDiffers from AkurasuNot on AkurasuSame as the original
Double move (W)Can act twice each turnGained when the pilot reaches the level set for each (see the pilot table below); the unit info on the map shows W while two actions remain this turnSame as the original
Kill-count funds bonusThe more kills your pilot has, the more funds you get for destroying enemies20–39 kills ×1.1, then +0.1 per 20 kills, ×2.0 from 200 kills; then multiplied with Fortune (up to ×4); at most 65,535 per unit destroyed; enemies don't get this bonus; experience isn't affected by kill countDiffers from AkurasuNot on AkurasuSame as the original
Limit (unit stat)Cap on hit/evasion plus mobilityBattle calculation never reads Limit at all: on the status screen an excess only changes color, and Limit upgrades, Limit-raising parts, and the Limit boosts from V-MAX and Super Mode have no effect in battleThe attacker's “hit + Mobility” and the defender's “evade + Mobility” are each capped at their unit's Limit; a high-level pilot in a low-grade unit loses noticeable hit and evade, which is what makes Limit upgrades and parts worthwhile
  • Both sides use the same rules: enemy ESP, Holy Warrior and Potential pilots are also calculated by this port's defaults
  • Critical rate = attacker's Skill − defender's Skill + weapon critical modifier, at least 1%; enemy attacks are further ÷4 and get no Potential bonus, so enemies almost never land criticals
  • Potential “halving” is backed only by community sources and unused data, weaker evidence than the other items; it can be turned off on its own if you don't like it
  • How skill level works: each pilot skill has 9 learn levels, and the skill level equals how many of them the pilot's current level has reached; NT, Enhanced, Holy Warrior, ESP and Potential share one level
  • EXP = (enemy pilot base EXP + enemy unit EXP) × level-difference factor (×3.4 when the enemy is 8+ levels higher, ×0.01 when 6+ levels lower); ÷10 without a kill, minimum 1; Gain ×2Not on Akurasu

How to switch Gameplay adjustments on and off

  • Open the settings in game and go to the “Rules” page: the “Corrections” group is on by default, the “Difficulty” group off by default
  • There are three presets: Restore defaults (corrections on, difficulty off), All off (original rules), All on
  • Changes take effect immediately, applying from the next battle resolution; the save format is unchanged, so you can switch rules on existing progress
  • 7 fixes in total: ESP, Holy Warrior evasion, Limit, Potential tiers, Potential halving, swap weapon carry-over, Hyper Aura Slash power
  • There are 5 Difficulty options: boss dummies halved, boss dummies none, upgrade cap, departure refund, parts carry over

Unit Status

Barrier abilities work very differently: Aura Barrier is “nothing unless pierced,” the I-Field types are “flat reduction, stackable,” and all of them work only against Beam shooting weapons and cost EN. Values and units come from ROM and battle code; the units listed after “Enemy” appear only on the enemy side.

Check order after a hit

  • Each attack first rolls to hit; only attacks that would hit go through these checks in order: Afterimage-type → Parry → Dummy → Barrier → Shield, stopping as soon as any one succeeds
  • So the Afterimage and Parry chances shown on screen are conditional probabilities “given a hit”
  • When the attacker uses Bullseye, Afterimage and Parry are skipped; Dummy, barriers and Shield are checked as usualDiffers from Akurasu
  • Barriers are checked only when the attacker uses a Beam shooting weapon and the defender has enough EN; once Aura Barrier is broken through, the I-Field types and Shield are no longer checkedNot on Akurasu
  • Damage is 0 when fully blocked by a barrier; otherwise minimum damage is 10

Dummy (enemy bosses only)

  • Some bosses have a number of Dummies: an attack that should hit is taken by the Dummy instead, the attack has no effect, and the count drops by 1; no roll, always works
  • Dummy is not used up when an attack is evaded or stopped by Afterimage or Parry; Dummy blocks attacks even when the attacker uses BullseyeDiffers from Akurasu
  • The game doesn't show the remaining count, and it doesn't recover between turns
  • In the original there are 42 deployment records with Dummy, all belonging to Haman, Char, Scirocco, Glemy, Milliardo, Gyunei, Gato and Le Cain, with 2, 3, 5 or 7 uses depending on the stage
  • Difficulty “Boss dummies: halved” changes 2/3/5/7 to 1/1/2/3; “Boss dummies: none” sets them to zero, and with both checked “none” wins; both off by default, and the new rule applies the next time a unit spawns
  • In the original, when Wufei appears as an enemy, his kill count from your side is used as his Dummy count; this port fixes that unconditionally, and he no longer has Dummy

Parts on unit swaps

  • In the original, a swap (including the stage where the new unit is auto-deployed right after) returns all of the old unit's parts to storage; the parts aren't lost, they just can't be re-equipped until the next intermission
  • Difficulty “Parts carry over” (off by default): on a unit swap, the old unit's parts go straight onto the new unit in their original order, and any that don't fit go to storage
  • The five Customs (Wing Zero, Sandrock, Deathscythe Hell, Heavyarms, Altron) and Shin Getter have only 1 part slot, while the previous units had 2, so each of these changes leaves one part in storage
  • Before and after the transformation Dancouga is the same unit upgraded in place; the original also removes its parts

Love bonus

Pairings come from the Love bonus table in ROM, with activation conditions from battle-code analysis. A pilot with the bonus deals +30% damage and takes −30% damage while the partner is within 2 squares (horizontal, vertical or diagonal, at most one square between).

  • The table above covers all 47 rows of the ROM's love bonus table: the table registers rows as “holder ← partner”, so two-way pairs take two rows; Zechs/Milliardo has 3 character IDs and Lady has 2, and Shiro and Aina are each registered twice, so there are more rows than pairs
  • Koji ↔ Maria and Duke ↔ Naida are both two-way: each table row has two partner columns, and the code checks both (an older version of this page listed them as one-way, which was a misreading)
  • In Super stages 2–6 (“Koji's Fury: Mazinger Rises!” through “Fearless! Le Cain's Challenge”), Koji and Sayaka get no bonus at all as holders, not even with Maria beside them; normal from stage 7 on
  • Treize ↔ Lady, not listed by AkurasuNot on Akurasu

Rules

  • Holder attacking → damage +30%; holder being attacked → damage taken −30%; hit rate unaffected
  • With multiple partners the bonus does not stack; at most ±30%
  • Effective only for ally pilots; the partner must also be an ally unit on the map
  • The partner must be within 2 squares of the holder: horizontal plus vertical distance of 2 or less (diagonally adjacent counts); it does not need to be on the current screenNot verified in game
  • The bonus applies after damage is calculated, before the Valor / Soul / critical multipliers

Upgrades and inheritance

SRW64's upgrade cap depends on the unit (6–15 levels): strong units get fewer, weak and mass-production units more. What else the cap determines

  • The five stats and every weapon of the unit share the same cap
  • When all five stats of each of the five W units are fully upgraded, it automatically becomes its custom version (only the five stats count, not weapons)
  • Some weapons unlock extra weapons when fully upgraded; see the “Extra weapons” page
  • Sale price of sellable mass-produced units = base price + 20,000 × the fraction of upgrade levels done out of the total upgradable
  • Each upgrade level in the save has only 4 bits, so 15 levels is the format's own cap

  • Inheritance happens only if the old unit is still on the team at that moment (regardless of who pilots it); after a swap the old unit is always deleted
  • The five stat levels carry over as a block, synced across Transform and combined forms; weapons carry over one by one per the game's mapping table, and weapons with no entry start from level 0; repair devices and combination attacks can't be upgraded anyway and are unaffected
  • Upgrade caps are not inherited; the new unit uses its own cap
  • The game's swap table also has Gundam Deathscythe → Gundam Deathscythe Hell, Gundam Heavyarms → Gundam Heavyarms Kai and Shenlong Gundam → Altron Gundam, but the story always deletes the old unit along with its pilot first, so these three swaps never actually inherit

Related optional rules

  • Fix “Machine swap: carry over three weapons the table misses” (on by default): adds the Flamethrower and Grenade Launcher for Layzner → New Layzner and the Dragon Fire for Altron Gundam → Custom; it takes effect only at the moment of the swap — turning it off later doesn't undo it, and turning it on doesn't backfill swaps that already happenedNot verified in game
  • Difficulty “Upgrade cap” (off by default): every unit can be upgraded to 15 on the upgrade screen, with cells beyond the original cap shown as ● (upgraded) / ☆ (not upgraded); Custom refits, extra weapon unlocks, sale prices, story-gifted levels and swap inheritance still use the original cap; levels already raised are kept if you turn it off, but can't be raised further
  • Difficulty “Departure refund” (off by default): when the story removes a unit from the team (leaving, the old unit deleted after a swap, the Godmars combination), the upgrade funds spent on it are refunded at current prices, with a notice at the top of the screen and in the dialogue log; selling and battlefield exits are not refunded; levels inherited by a new unit and story-gifted levels are not refunded, but levels a unit brings when it joins are
  • For how parts are handled in unit swaps, see the “Parts” page

Extra weapons

Some weapons unlock new weapons when upgraded to the unit's cap; the Earthgain, Virose and Super Earthgain attacks unlock with pilot level; and a batch of finishers unlocks through the story. Unlock tables, weapon values and use conditions all come from ROM and code analysis; story unlock timing comes from script analysis.

Combination attacks

Participation conditions, multipliers and values all come from the ROM's combination attack data and check code. A combination attack appears in the weapon list only when every participant meets its Will and EN requirements and they are connected on the map (diagonal adjacency counts; with three or more units, the group just needs to be connected as a whole, not every pair adjacent), and any participant can launch it. Attack power = the average of the current attack power (including upgrades) of each participating unit's corresponding component attack × multiplier, rounded down. Each participant pays the combination attack's EN once; no ammo is used.

GB link

The original needs the 64GB Pak connected to the GB game Super Robot Wars Link Battler for F91, GoShogun and Zambot 3 to join. This port needs no cartridge: just check the series on the intermission screen. Unlock conditions, link stages and join levels all come from analysis of the ROM, scripts and code.

  • Each Link stage has a ground and a space version, chosen by whether the originally scheduled next stage is in space

How Link works in this port

  • Pick “Link” in the intermission menu to open the Link page: three series cards; check the series to add, then “Next: Link”
  • Card states: joined (grayed out, can't be selected again), scheduled (the next stage is already the link stage; the checkbox is locked), available
  • Then the original “GB Link” screen opens as usual; press B to return to the intermission menu
  • The matching link stage is inserted before the next battle, with the newly joining characters on your side; afterwards you return to the originally scheduled next stage
  • Link stage defeat condition: the game is over if a newly joined character is destroyed
  • The original link pulls the experience of pilots shared by both games up to the higher of the two; this port's virtual cartridge mirrors your own pilots directly, so nobody's level changes

Other

  • After a Link, some later stages have extra dialogue for these characters
  • Once Zambot 3 joins, it can use the combination attack “Space Combination Attack” with the Daitarn 3
  • After a Link, the title screen's Sound Test gains “F91ガンダム出撃”, “行けザンボット3” and “ゴーショーグン発進せよ”, and Karaoke gains two songs for the Zambot 3 and GoShogun; the condition is that these units have been on the team, not the Link itselfNot on Akurasu
  • A newly joined pilot's level = team average level + 1 (Cecily gets the average); the average is taken over the 15 highest-level pilots on the team who are assigned to units, rounded down, capped at 95 and at stages cleared + 40Not on AkurasuNot verified in game
